scope: A curated starting collection of public reporting from Ballard and Alki. Not a complete Seattle incident database.

incidents.summary: An attempted entry was reported at about 4:30 a.m. Owners shared surveillance footage and asked neighbors for help.
incidents.details: Owners believe the same people and van appeared in the September incident. That connection and any links to other businesses have not been independently confirmed.

incidents.summary: Owners reported a break-in at approximately 2:30 a.m., later sharing footage alongside a November attempted entry.
incidents.details: The November report is the source for both incidents. No dollar estimate was reported.

incidents.summary: Money, an employee's laptop and a speaker were taken without broken glass or apparent forced entry.
incidents.details: Owner Ben Libay estimated $800-$1,000 in losses, below the insurance deductible, and said he did not file a police report.

incidents.summary: Two people damaged a lockbox and gate, took a key and fob, and attempted entry through a sidewalk door.
incidents.details: The owner said they did not enter the cafe. A baker was already on-site. The report describes surveillance footage but gives no repair estimate.

incidents.summary: A front window was smashed with a rock. Staff described the incident in surveillance footage.
incidents.details: Copine had installed security film after a previous break-in. That earlier, undated event is context only and is not separately counted. This window damage is classified as vandalism, not burglary.

incidents.summary: An outdoor refrigeration unit was destroyed and stripped of copper, with losses reported above $25,000.
incidents.details: Owner Sam Thompson reported no insurance coverage for the damage and two attempted entries the following night. Those undated attempts are noted here but not separately counted. The article links an owner fundraiser.

incidents.summary: A person entered the lobby around 1:45 a.m. and took coins, keys, an iPad and third-party tablets.
incidents.details: No windows were broken. The owner said a lock had been loosened during an earlier attempted entry. That earlier event is not separately counted because its date was not reported.

incidents.summary: Glass in the front door was shattered and cargo vans were damaged, costing an estimated $5,000.
incidents.details: The owner described the incident retrospectively in May 2026. A further roughly $1,000 in alarms and unspecified fence and staffing costs are not included in the incident loss total.

incidents.summary: A window was smashed and a door was attacked with a crowbar. Management estimated about $600 in damage.
incidents.details: The source calls this a break-in. Management said the storefront is cashless and wanted to preserve a welcoming atmosphere.

incidents.summary: Police said burglars kicked in the door shortly after 1 a.m. Nothing was reported stolen.
incidents.details: The manager estimated up to $5,000 in damage. An upper-only estimate is displayed but not added to the documented cost floor. Police had not confirmed a link to the nearby coffee shop incident.

incidents.summary: A bag of tools valued at about $200 was stolen roughly half an hour after the Five Guys burglary.
incidents.details: Police had not confirmed that the same suspects were involved in the two incidents.

incidents.summary: Surveillance showed a bolt being cut before entry. The co-owner reported a stolen register, cash and a safe.
incidents.details: The adjoining coffee and ice cream businesses are treated as one shared location. FOX 13 described three separate months of incidents, not three incidents at each business.

incidents.summary: Burglars forced the glass doors of the Ben & Jerry's shop and took a safe.
incidents.details: The co-owner said the adjoining shops subsequently went cashless. No dollar estimate for this incident was provided.

incidents.summary: A further entry after the businesses went cashless resulted in a stolen iPad and about $1,000 in damage.
incidents.details: The source attributes the $1,000 to damage, not the value of the iPad. No stolen cash was reported in this incident.

incidents.summary: Burglars forced an emergency exit, damaged cameras and took iPads and irreplaceable gifts from customers.
incidents.details: The February 19 report says the incident occurred on Wednesday, giving an inferred date of February 18. The owners said they filed a police report and remained open at the time of reporting. No loss estimate was published.
